description: Progressive provides insurance for a wide range of personal and business assets. The company is divided into three units. The personal division insures cars and recreational vehicles, while the commercial arm writes policies for businesses to cover their liability and vehicle fleets, including freight trucks. The third unit handles property insurance, including home and rental coverage. Progressive was founded in 1937.

title: Progressive

rankings.title: 100 Best Large Workplaces for Women
rankings.itemDescription:
Employees say:

"The people make Progressive. I have always found Progressive to be an inclusive, collaborative, and caring work environment. The leadership team is relatable and approachable. Progressive celebrates its employees and also communicates from the top about current events or situations affecting the country, often offering a reassuring word and positive message, which is appreciated in uncertain times. One of the most cherished events is our Keys to Progress program giving back to Veterans with the car giveaway event. I am proud to work for a company that recognizes Veterans and their sacrifices for our country and freedom."

rankings.title: Best Large Workplaces in Financial Services and Insurance
rankings.itemDescription:
Employees say: 

"Progressive is a place where I know I will most likely be for the rest of my career. I have met the best people as longtime friends. I am able to learn different skills. I knew nothing about insurance. I started in customer service, then insurance verification, then senior underwriter and now a senior resolution specialist. I am able to literally message or email our CEO and she answers each time. I have referred three people to Progressive, and they love it. This place sincerely cares about me and my mental and physical health. I have purchased my first home working here. I have never enjoyed coming to work until Progressive.  I have always wanted to work at Progressive and nine years in, I couldn't be happier."

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription:

"Progressive really makes everyone feel welcome, supported and safe to be themselves. During difficult times in the world, I feel protected knowing that this is my workplace - I feel confident that the company will stay strong in representing our values and I feel like I have a great deal of security in knowing the company will do whatever it can to keep people employed. I can say that we truly have a great group of people that don't just come to work to do their jobs but also take extra time to know who you are as a person and make you feel loved."

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription:
Progressive’s Inclusion Quarterly initiative features speakers and discussion groups, and encourages storytelling and sharing. A weeklong inclusion program in 2022 attracted 32,269 employees, who attended programming on topics such as thriving in a digital workplace and using emotional intelligence to nurture relationships and trust.
 

Since its workplace shifted to 90% remote and hybrid over the pandemic, the insurer’s staff have increasingly relied on its intracompany social media platform to connect and share stories; 4,500 employees joined the platform in 2022.
 

Every Progressive worker is eligible to recommend that any charity receive a $100 donation from the Progressive Insurance Foundation. In 2023 the company expanded its donation program to include national nonprofit Family Promise, which, alongside Progressive’s ongoing collaboration with the Cleveland operations of Humble Design, represents the company’s particular commitment to ending homelessness in the U.S.

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription:
A leading provider of auto, vehicle, and homeowner insurance in the U.S., Progressive says that 96% of its employees agree with the following statement: “When you join the company, you are made to feel welcome.”

  • Within the past two years, Progressive says, it has increased the representation of people of color among senior leadership from 13% to 17%. And at the end of 2022, it says, 45% of those in leadership positions were women and 25% were people of color.

  • The Multicultural Leadership Development Program is a 12-to-18-month training to help higher-performing employees prepare for managerial positions.

  • All employees have access to PrudentRx, which lets members avoid out-of-pocket expenses for all approved specialty medications in Progressive’s health plan.

  • “They are transparent and seek to create a work environment where people of all backgrounds can collaborate and work together. I truly feel valued and appreciated,” said one employee.

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription:
The fifth largest property and casualty insurer in the Fortune 500, Progressive’s performance in 2022 was mixed, with a 4% increase in revenue but a 79% decrease in profit compared to the prior year, and it dropped nine places on the Fortune 500.

  • Auto claims stabilized in 2022 after first dropping in 2020 because of stay-at-home initiatives and then jumping up in 2021 as drivers returned to the road.

  • Hurricane Ian, which struck Florida and South Carolina in September 2022, ate into Progressive’s bottom line. For all insurers, the massive storm caused the second-largest insured loss on record after Hurricane Katrina in 2005.

  • Progressive is one of the 52 Fortune 500 companies that have women leaders, with Tricia Griffith as president and CEO. Progressive is one of the few companies with a female board chair: Lawton W. Fitt, a retired Goldman Sachs partner.

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription: Telling employees they’re valued is one thing, but Progressive takes extra pains to show its 44,915 workers how crucial they are to the success of the company. Its annual Gainsharing Incentive plan financially rewards employees—not just executives—for both individual and team success. The insurance company has a strong diversity and inclusion focus, with one worker saying it “acknowledges all, regardless of gender, ethnic background, sexual orientation, or disabilities.” It plans to double the representation of people of color in senior leadership by the end of 2025. And nearly half of all Progressive employees are members of at least one Employee Resource Groups, with many belonging to multiple groups.

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription: Progressive is the third-largest auto insurance carrier in the U.S. by market share, and the largest insurer of commercial vehicles. As more cars got back on the road in 2021, the economy’s rebound from the pandemic was a mixed blessing for Progressive. The company recorded an 11% year-over-year revenue increase, but a 41% year-over-year decrease in profits—since more driving meant more accidents and more insurance claims.

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription: Though drivers were stuck at home for much of the year, Progressive’s business remained in high gear. The company did not lay off or furlough workers, and even offered personal auto customers 20% rebates in May and June of 2020. One employee appreciated that Progressive modified its bonus schedule to pay out quarterly rather than at year-end, a move that helped families who might have experienced a job loss. Says one veteran of the Fortune 500 company, led by Tricia Griffith, who was Fortune’s 2018 Businessperson of the Year: “Progressive is by far the best place I’ve ever worked.”

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: Car travel may have all but stalled for much of 2020, but Progressive nonetheless gained a windfall of business—with policies increasing by 2.4 million and an additional $3 billion in net premiums written over the prior year. The company’s agency auto business and Uber and Lyft premiums decreased because of shelter-in-place restrictions and decreased circulation. Yet the insurer’s commercial lines business saw significant growth in the for-hire transportation business, spurred on by increased demand for shipping services.

Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: Progressive had a big year: With revenues climbing 22% year-over-year, profits jumping 52%, and more than 4,000 new employees hired, the insurer catapulted up 68 spots on the Global 500. Progressive’s growth was aided by its commercial lines segment, which grew 20% year-over-year. The House that Flo Built also expanded its auto coverage with ridesharing titans Uber and Lyft. In early 2020, stay-at-home orders dramatically lowered domestic traffic, and thus auto insurance claims. As a result, CEO Tricia Griffith—who, in 2018, was the first woman to be named Fortune’s Businessperson of the Year—announced that the company would refund its insured drivers 20% of their April and May premiums.
